title: Architect: checking a design against crew constraints
when: A proposed design or plan may need things the crew cannot use: packages, a build step, a remote service, a database server.
prompt:
Goal: Every part of the design confirmed to run as plain files with no install and no network, with a local replacement for anything that would not.
Steps:
1. Read the plan and list every external need: packages, CDNs, fonts, APIs, servers, compilers, bundlers.
2. Check each against the rules: plain static files, relative paths, vanilla JS modules, Node and Python standard libraries only, no network.
3. Replace each violation with a local equivalent: system font stack, inline SVG icons, localStorage or a JSON file, node:http, node:test, fetch of a local file.
4. Check browser features: ES modules from file:// need a local server, so say how to start one with node or python -m http.server.
5. Check data rules: nothing leaves the machine, nothing requires an account.
6. Write a note listing each replacement and any feature that had to change.
Quality bar:
- No remaining external dependency.
- Every replacement keeps the feature working.
- Run instructions match the final design.
Pitfalls:
- A font or icon link left in the head.
- Assuming fetch of a JSON file works from file:// without a server.
- Replacing a needed feature with nothing and not saying so.
Verify:
- [ ] No http or https URLs in code files.
- [ ] No import of a package name without node: prefix.
- [ ] Storage is local.
- [ ] Changes are noted.
Output: A note with the constraint review and edits to the plan or files that remove violations.

examples.input: plan says use a charting package and a web font
examples.output: replace with Canvas bars in chart.js and a system font stack; note both
